title: Yareba, Middle Musa in Papua New Guinea
text: The Yareba language is part of the Yareban family within the Trans-New Guinea language group and is used by the community in daily communication. While Tok Pisin and English may be encountered in regional schools and markets, the Yareba language remains predominant in village life.

title: Yareba language — Grokipedia
text: Yareba, also known as Middle Musa, is a Trans-New Guinea language spoken by approximately 800 to 1,200 people in the Ijivitari and Popondetta districts of Oro Province, Papua New Guinea, particularly along the Middle Musa River valley. title: Yareba Language (YRB) - L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level ...
text: Yareba is a stable indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
